title: Workload-aware batching defaults (beta) — customer cohort plan (Optimize)
content:
Last updated: 2025-03-18 (Aditya)

Purpose
- Define a small, high-signal beta cohort for “workload-aware batching defaults” (tiered batching profiles: fast / standard / cost-efficient).
- Align on success criteria, comms, and which accounts/routes we will enable.
- Make it easy for SE/CS to track: who is in, what they’re testing, what we’re watching, and how we decide to expand.

Beta summary (what customers will experience)
- New config option: batching_tier = fast | standard | cost_efficient.
- “Standard” is the recommended default for most non-streaming chat/completions routes unless customers have strict token-cadence requirements.
- “Fast” prioritizes low queue delay / tail latency; “cost-efficient” prioritizes throughput and $/token with stronger overload protection.
- We will enable via feature flag and/or explicit opt-in per project / route.

Primary goals for beta
1) Validate tier behavior holds across a representative set of real workloads.
2) Verify that “cost-efficient” produces meaningful savings without unacceptable error/timeout increases.
3) Ensure streaming cadence is not degraded by fast/standard tiers (token cadence + perceived responsiveness).
4) Validate customer-facing explanation: customers understand trade-offs and can troubleshoot via effective-config + dashboards.

Non-goals for beta
- Per-customer bespoke tuning beyond tier selection + a small number of safe overrides.
- Support for every model/region on day 1 (we will start with a subset).

Entry criteria (who should be in the beta)
Must-have
- Clear objective: reduce cost per 1M tokens and/or stabilize p95 latency.
- Willing to run A/B or staged traffic split for 1–2 weeks.
- Has observability access (either Redwood Console or agrees to share request IDs + exported metrics).
- Workload fits one of the initial supported buckets:
  - Chat/completions (streaming or non-streaming)
  - Embeddings (non-streaming; batch-friendly)

Nice-to-have
- Mix of deployment types (Hosted + Dedicated; one Private if low risk and easy rollback).
- Mix of workload shapes (short prompts, long context, tool calls, high concurrency spikes).

Do NOT include (for beta phase 1)
- Accounts with frequent incident history around timeouts where we can’t do a clean rollback.
- Ultra latency-sensitive streaming where token cadence is a contractual requirement (unless they explicitly want to test fast tier only).
- Customers actively changing models/regions weekly (too many confounders).

Supported scope for initial cohort (phase 1)
- Deployment: Hosted API (primary), Dedicated (select accounts), Private (phase 2).
- Regions: us-east + eu-west (initial). Others by exception.
- Models: top 3–5 chat models + primary embeddings model (exact list maintained in runtime launch brief).

Success criteria (measured per route, by tier)
Technical
- p95 latency delta vs baseline (customer’s prior config) stays within tier contract:
  - fast: p95 regression <= 0% (goal: improve), p99 regression <= 5%
  - standard: p95 regression <= 5%, p99 regression <= 10%
  - cost-efficient: p95 regression <= 15%, p99 regression <= 20%
- Queue delay: stable and not “spiky” (watch p95 queue_delay_ms + long tails).
- Errors: no sustained increase in 5xx, timeouts, cancels (alert thresholds per SRE).
- Streaming: token cadence / time-to-first-token (TTFT) does not regress beyond agreed threshold for routes on streaming.

Business / value
- cost-efficient tier delivers >= 10% reduction in $/1M tokens (target 15–25%) for at least one meaningful production route.
- standard tier delivers more predictable p95 (reduction in variance) at similar unit cost.

Customer acceptance
- Customer can articulate which tier they chose and why.
- Support load does not materially increase; if it does, we produce a troubleshooting playbook + docs fixes.

Exit criteria (who “graduates”)
- Ran at least 5 days at >= 10% traffic on a production route (or a full-traffic POC environment with real load).
- Signed off on observed trade-offs and wants to keep tiered batching enabled.

Cohort plan (waves)
Wave 0 — Internal/dogfood (already in progress)
- Redwood internal services running on Hosted.
- Goal: shake out obvious regressions + make sure effective-config and metrics are sufficient.

Wave 1 — External beta (5–8 accounts)
- Mix: 2 cost-focused startups, 1 mid-market SaaS, 1 enterprise eval, 1 embeddings-heavy customer.
- Enablement: explicit opt-in, per-route.

Wave 2 — Expansion (10–20 accounts)
- Add Dedicated + one “friendly” Private install (only if feature flag + rollback proven).

Candidate accounts (proposed)
Columns:
- Account / Segment / Deployment / Primary routes / Workload notes / Proposed tier(s) / Expected value / Risk flags / Owner (Redwood) / Next step / Links

1) VertexWave (Company ID 10441)
- Segment: mid-market SaaS (cost-down initiative)
- Deployment: Hosted API (us-east)
- Primary routes: chat streaming (user-facing), chat non-streaming (batch jobs)
- Workload notes:
  - Peaks during business hours; concurrency spikes.
  - Mixed prompt lengths; some tool-calls.
  - Strong interest in cost-efficient but nervous about perceived latency.
- Proposed tier(s):
  - Start: standard on non-streaming route
  - Pilot: cost-efficient on batch route only
  - Keep: fast or standard for streaming route depending on cadence results
- Expected value: 15–25% $/token savings on batch route; stabilize p95 under spikes
- Risk flags: streaming cadence sensitivity; may over-generalize results if applied to all routes
- Owner: Miguel Santos (CS), Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API partner)
- Next step: confirm success metrics + A/B plan; schedule enablement window
- Links:
  - HubSpot: hubspot:company-10441-vertexwave
  - Fireflies: fireflies:sales-calls/ff-2025-02-14-vertexwave-technical-deep-dive
  - Email follow-up: gmail:aditya_rao/thread-20250215T091233Z-vertexwave-followup

2) LuminaAI (Company ID 10488)
- Segment: AI-native startup (POC)
- Deployment: Dedicated (planned) / Hosted (during POC)
- Primary routes: chat non-streaming (agent runs), embeddings (indexing)
- Workload notes:
  - Embeddings-heavy workloads are batch-friendly.
  - Chat is less latency-sensitive (background agent) but sensitive to timeouts.
- Proposed tier(s):
  - embeddings: cost-efficient
  - chat non-streaming: standard
- Expected value: 20%+ savings on embeddings throughput; clearer story for “choose tier per route”
- Risk flags: POC environment changes; may switch models mid-test
- Owner: Henry Cho (product), Miguel Santos (CS)
- Next step: include tier selection in POC plan + dashboard walk-through
- Links:
  - HubSpot: hubspot:company-10488-luminaai
  - Fireflies: fireflies:sales-calls/ff-2025-02-28-luminaai-poc-scoping

3) Existing customer (name redacted in this doc — see CS notes)
- Segment: enterprise (existing)
- Deployment: Hosted API (eu-west)
- Primary routes: chat streaming + occasional long-context
- Workload notes:
  - Reported small regressions during early ramp; we paused rollout once.
  - Strong partner for feedback but requires careful change management.
- Proposed tier(s):
  - fast for streaming route only
  - standard for non-streaming
- Expected value: validate fast tier cadence behavior in eu-west
- Risk flags: prior regression; must have strict rollback threshold and comms plan
- Owner: Rafael Mendes (SRE on-call lead), Miguel Santos (CS)
- Next step: re-run with updated scheduler fixes + stricter monitoring
- Links:
  - Fireflies: fireflies:customer-success/ff-2025-03-12-existing-customer-beta-checkin

4) (Placeholder) Embeddings-heavy SaaS customer — needs nomination
- Segment: mid-market
- Deployment: Hosted API
- Primary routes: embeddings indexing + periodic re-index
- Workload notes: stable and highly batchable; ideal for cost-efficient validation
- Proposed tier(s): cost-efficient on embeddings
- Expected value: clean unit economics win; minimal user-visible latency sensitivity
- Risk flags: ensure no increased timeout rate during re-index spikes
- Owner: TBD (CS)
- Next step: Miguel to nominate 2–3 candidates by 2025-03-22

5) (Optional, phase 2) Friendly Private deployment
- Segment: regulated-ish customer with private control plane
- Deployment: Private (VPC)
- Primary routes: chat non-streaming
- Proposed tier(s): standard
- Risk flags: migration complexity; must align with installer/helm support
- Owner: Diego Santos (config propagation), Connor O’Brien (release)
- Next step: only after wave 1 meets success criteria

Open questions / decisions needed
- Naming: “cost-efficient” vs “eco” (strong preference from product thread: keep “cost-efficient” in docs; “eco” may appear as short label in UI only if we must).
- Default behavior in Hosted: do we set standard as default for select models/regions during beta, or keep opt-in only? (current recommendation: opt-in only for wave 1; consider default-on for new projects only in wave 2).
- Customer troubleshooting: do we have a single “effective config” endpoint surfaced in Console before wave 1? (blocker for customers who are confused about tier vs explicit overrides; see SUP-18510).

Messaging (beta invite blurb — draft)
Subject: Beta: simpler batching profiles to reduce cost (with SLO-friendly guardrails)

Hi <name>,
We’re running a limited beta of workload-aware batching defaults in Redwood Inference. You can now choose a batching tier per route (fast / standard / cost-efficient) and Redwood will apply a safe set of scheduling and batching defaults optimized for your workload shape.

What you get:
- Faster onboarding vs manual tuning
- Better throughput and lower $/1M tokens (especially on cost-efficient for batch-friendly routes)
- Clear guardrails and rollback controls

How the beta works:
- Opt in per project/route; we start at 10% traffic and ramp.
- We’ll share a dashboard checklist (latency, queue delay, batch formation, timeouts).
- You can opt out instantly (feature flag rollback) and keep your existing explicit batching settings.

If you’re interested, reply with:
- which routes you want to test (streaming vs non-streaming)
- your latency expectations (p95 target)
- preferred time window for enablement

— Aditya (Optimize)

Customer-facing “positioning bullets” (for SE/CS)
- “Choose the tier that matches your SLO and cost goals; Redwood handles the safe defaults.”
- “Fast protects p95/p99; cost-efficient maximizes throughput and unit economics with overload protection.”
- “You can still override specific knobs; explicit config wins over tier defaults.”
- “We expose effective configuration so you can see what’s applied and why.”

Operational plan (how we run the beta)
- Enablement steps (per account/route)
  1) Confirm target route(s), streaming/non-streaming, baseline p95/p99 + timeout rates.
  2) Decide tier(s); confirm if any explicit overrides are currently set.
  3) Start at 10% traffic; monitor 60–120 min.
  4) Ramp to 25% then 50% then 100% over 3–5 days if stable.
  5) Capture end-of-week summary: metrics + qualitative feedback.

- Monitoring checklist (minimum)
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 by route + tier label
  - queue_delay_ms (p95/p99)
  - Batch size distribution (mean + p95)
  - GPU util / saturation proxy (Hosted: runtime-reported utilization)
  - Error rates: timeouts, cancels, 5xx
  - Streaming: TTFT + token cadence proxy (if available)

- Rollback triggers (for beta)
  - p95 latency regression sustained > tier threshold for 30 min (after excluding deploy events)
  - timeout rate increase > 2x baseline for 15 min
  - customer reports user-visible degradation on streaming (treat as immediate pause)

Risks + mitigations (what we should be explicit about)
- Risk: cost-efficient can increase queue delay under bursty concurrency.
  - Mitigation: overload protection alignment + strict rollback thresholds.
- Risk: streaming cadence regressions if decode prioritization is wrong.
  - Mitigation: keep streaming on fast/standard initially; require cadence check before expanding cost-efficient to streaming.
- Risk: confusion about tier vs explicit overrides.
  - Mitigation: docs + “effective config” surfaced; proactive message: “explicit overrides win.” (track SUP-18510)

Notes from Support / CS (beta readiness feedback)
- SUP-18492: one customer reported increased timeouts when trying cost-efficient.
  - Action: require overload protection PRs to be present before cost-efficient expands; add troubleshooting steps + “what to look at” (timeouts vs queue delay vs capacity).
- SUP-18510: confusion about why changing tier didn’t change behavior (they had explicit overrides).
  - Action: add effective-config view + docs callout + Console copy.

Asks / next steps
- CS/SE: nominate 2 additional embeddings-heavy candidates by 2025-03-22.
- SRE (Sean/Rafael): confirm tier p95/p99 thresholds for beta monitoring doc; sign off on rollback triggers.
- DevEx (Monica/Elliot): confirm docs language for “cost-efficient” and finalize public FAQ before wave 1 ramp.
- Product (Aditya): finalize wave 1 list and send invites by 2025-03-25.

Changelog
- 2025-03-18: Added support-ticket learnings and tightened entry criteria for streaming routes.
- 2025-03-10: Added LuminaAI and clarified embeddings plan.
- 2025-02-13: Initial draft created after VertexWave deep dive scheduling.
